data.note: Reserved slots in the plan cut, adapter port, knobs, reporting through summary and parallel line

data.claim: The cap exists only in plan()'s cut (claim does not apply it to a named item), so the reservation belongs in the optimizer cut; and next, status and brief all print strings core owns (Plan.summary, Plan.parallel_line), so reporting needs no surface file.
data.falsifier: A cap check inside claim, or a next/status/brief renderer printing the limit from anything other than Plan.summary or Plan.parallel_line.
data.mechanism: Ordinary work may hold at most cap minus reserved slots; a single walk in offer order with one extra per-class limit keeps priority order, and the total cap already covers bug fixes that overflow the reserved share.

chunk_findings.detail: `kept_out` items are appended to `p.capped`, then `p.cap_note` (already set to `the worktree cap ({cap})` just before `_cut_ready`) is only suffixed with ` and schedule.reserved_slots`. `Plan.summary` reports every capped id as held by that note. Input: worktree cap 2, `reserved_slots` 1, one ordinary item already live, one ordinary ready item the optimizer marks `reserved` (idle reserved slot still free). Summary becomes `1 held by the worktree cap (2) and schedule.reserved_slots` even though the cap is not reached — the case the new comment cites as never "cap reached" (B40386f7a40). `next`/`status`/`brief` therefore blame the worktree cap for a reservation hold.

chunk_findings.detail: When `reserved_slots`/`reserved_tags` are configured and `plan(parallel=...)` is passed, `_plan.py` sets `p.parallel_line` to `line` already joined with `p.reserved_note`. `Plan.summary` already includes `self.parallel_line`, and this change also appends `self.reserved_note` as a separate summary part. That makes one summary emit the same reserved note twice, e.g. `parallel: 4 (fixed); schedule.reserved_slots: 1` and then later `schedule.reserved_slots: 1` in the same output.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule/_plan.py:p.parallel_line + ddflow/core/schedule/_readiness.py:Plan.summary

chunk_findings.detail: `share` for the regular cap is computed with `len(ordinary)`, where `ordinary` is every non-reserved live item, including worktree leases (line 59 relies on the same list to count `.worktree` items). Worktree leases consume `cfg.worktree.max_parallel`, not the regular `limit`, so they must be excluded when computing the regular ordinary allowance. Example: `cfg.worktree.enabled=True`, `limit=4`, `cfg.schedule.reserved_slots=2`, one live ordinary worktree item, and no regular live items. The regular cap should still allow `ordinary_free(4, 2, 0)=2` ordinary flight tasks, but `len(ordinary)=1` gives `share=1`; with two worktree items `share=0`. The returned `Slots(..., min(share, flight), ...)` then caps the normal cut at 0/1 instead of 2, starving ordinary features the reservation rule says may run.

CHECK: a task inherits the needs of its phase, so read the phase needs before placing a task; a wrong …</ddflow-record>
The newly added test file `tests/test_reserved_slots.py` implements test helper functions like `_task` that add tasks to logs without including a wave tag or explicit `needs` dependencies/`no-deps` tags, violating the rule [r-task-phase-needs-wave] which mandates that every task carries a wave:N tag or a no-deps tag and states dependencies in needs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_reserved_slots.py:16

chunk_findings.detail: `open_slots` treats every non-reserved live lease as consuming the parallel cap (`ordinary_free(limit, wanted, len(ordinary))`), but a worktree lease does not count against that cap. With limit 2, `reserved_slots` 1 (ordinary may hold 1), and one ordinary worktree task already leased, `flight` is still 2 while `share` becomes `ordinary_free(2, 1, 1) = 0`, so the offer hands out no ordinary parallel slot even though parallel occupancy is 0. The same count is used by `idle_reserved` via `_flying` (every live lease): limit 4, `reserved_slots` 2, two ordinary worktree tasks and nothing on the parallel limit yields `ordinary_free == 0` and `idle == 2`, so `binding` is `2 + 2 >= 4` and the adaptive limit grows though no parallel slot is in use.
